transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-29
Time: 14:30 PDT
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Marta Gomez (LyraHealth), Samir Patel (LyraHealth SRE), Aisha Khan (LyraHealth ML), Don Lee (LyraHealth Security)

Summary:
Quick hands-on workshop of Redwood's Trace Inspector feature set for request debugging, error analysis, and request log correlation. Focus on how to find bad responses, correlate root cause (model variant, KV cache miss, routing fallback), and export actionable artifacts for engineering. Discussed Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs for LyraHealth's compliance and latency goals.

Topics covered:
- Request trace layout and timeline view
- Error classification and automated anomaly tagging
- KV cache / prefix cache inspection & hit/miss analysis
- Routing & fallback chain visibility (model variant/routing policy)
- Exporting traces for post-mortem and bench harnessing
- Security controls: audit trail, retention, SSO/SAML, KMS note

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (AE): alright everyone thanks for joining, we'll run about an hour, earlier than I expected but we can go deep, Priya and Liam are gonna drive the trace walk-through.
[00:18] Marta (LyraHealth): thanks, quick ask — we're primarily looking to reduce time to debug model hallucinations for clinical summaries, and keep PII out of logs, so would love to see the tracing and export controls.
[00:30] Priya (SE): absolutely, great context Marta. quick note: we'll show the Trace Inspector UI and then jump into a few real request traces we pulled from a sanitized queue — those are links in the chat, see "sanitized-trace-2025-08-20.json".
[00:45] Samir (SRE): are those full payloads or redacted? we need assurance PII is not present.
[00:52] Priya (SE): redacted, we scrubbed protected fields and used tokenization on PHI — the export pipeline strips configured keys via the redact policy. there is also a retained raw only for customer-managed KMS in Private deployments.
[01:10] Don (Security): that KMS remark — can you spell out how KMS ties into the private plane? sometimes your docs say private control plane, other times its an appliance.
[01:22] Liam (SE): sure, quick clarifier: for Private we offer a customer-managed KMS integration where master keys never leave your VPC or HSM. audit logs show key use events. in Hosted we encrypt at rest with our managed keys but you can opt for bring-your-own-key for dedicated plans.
[01:40] Jordan (AE): ok jumping into the UI — Priya, can you share your screen?
[01:45] Priya (SE): sharing now — alright you should see the Request Timeline. top-left there's the request header, timestamp, route, model variant. you can scrub to see token-level timing and KV cache operations.
[02:05] [Priya shares screen, brief pause]
[02:12] Priya (SE): note — transcription here sometimes shows K V cache as letters separated, that comes from the ASR; ignore the space. you can see an example trace where latency spikes at token 46.
[02:28] Marta (LyraHealth): can you filter to only traces with error code 502 or explicit generation cutoff?
[02:35] Priya (SE): yep filter at the top, and you can stack filters — status: 502, model: redwood-7b-quant, kv_hit:false. the UI also highlights likely regressions flagged by our anomaly detector.
[02:50] Samir (SRE): interesting, how do you attribute an error to a model variant vs infra? we get a lot of noisy fallbacks.
[03:00] Priya (SE): good question — we show a routing chain: primary model -> fallback model -> region fallback. each hop includes the reason (OOM, timeout, capacity-limit). errors will annotate where the failure happened, and we surface per-hop logs including kernel errors or orchestration retries. sometimes the ASR will say "essay el ay" instead of SLA — ignore that, sorry.
[03:28] Aisha (ML): can I see the logits or token choices to debug hallucination?
[03:33] Priya (SE): we expose token deltas in the debug view, there's a toggle to show candidate token scores (approx, not raw fp32 unless you run Private with debug enabled). that's often enough to see why a model switched tack mid-generation.
[03:50] [05:00] Speaker 4: sorry slight crosstalk as someone's dog barked
[05:10] Priya (SE): no problem — jumping to an error example: here's a clinical summary request where the model abruptly cut off. you can see a KV cache miss at the prefix stage, leading to longer decode times and a route fallback to a cheaper variant. the system annotated the fallthrough.
[05:36] Samir (SRE): so that was a cache miss causing latency and then triggering fallback. can we set policy to prefer latency over cost to avoid that?
[05:45] Liam (SE): yes you can pin routing policies per-route, e.g., prefer-low-latency: true, and that routes to dedicated pools or higher tier variants, with a cost multiplier shown in the policy UI.
[06:02] Marta (LyraHealth): curious about retention — we are regulated in EU and want 90 day retention only, no long term. can we configure per-workspace retention?
[06:12] Priya (SE): yes per-workspace retention is supported. in Private you control retention via your own S3 buckets, in Hosted we provide retention controls and certified deletion endpoints. we'll include the retention SLA in the security brief.
[06:30] Jordan (AE): folks want to see an export, Priya can you export this trace and show what the artifact looks like?
[06:36] Priya (SE): exporting now — the export contains request metadata, token timings, KV ops, and compacted model logs. by default PII keys are redacted; you can toggle include_raw for Private trials. download link posted in chat.
[07:05] Aisha (ML): how big are these traces? at scale this could be heavy to store.
[07:12] Liam (SE): trace size depends on token length and debug verbosity. we have a compression and retention tiering: hot traces (30 days full detail) and archived summaries (tokens + metrics only). Optimize suggests what to keep based on anomaly scoring.
[07:35] Marta (LyraHealth): about anomaly scoring — is that customizable? we have domain-specific failure modes.
[07:42] Priya (SE): yes you can upload custom test prompts and define baselines. anomalies are relative to those baselines, and you can train a lightweight classifier for domain signals.
[08:00] Jordan (AE): quick commercial note — if you go Dedicated we can schedule a pilot with capacity guarantees. we'll follow up with pricing numbers.
[08:12] Don (Security): before commercial, one more security ask — can trace exports be ingested only by S3 with encryption + object-level retention? we cannot allow exports to public buckets.
[08:24] Priya (SE): yes we support direct S3 delivery into your account for Private and Dedicated. exports to third-party integrations are opt-in. all transport is TLS and objects are encrypted with your KMS key if configured.
[08:40] [10:00] Priya (SE): jumping to a different trace — this one has repeated hallucinations where the model adds fictional medications. here you'll see token probability dips before the hallucination starts, then a long tail of low-probability tokens. we correlate that with the system prompt change and a large prefix token insertion.
[10:25] Aisha (ML): so prompt drift is measurable? can you annotate when system prompt changes across revisions?
[10:33] Priya (SE): yes, trace inspector shows prompt diffs and a quick timeline of model config changes. you can also attach git hashes from your prompt manager if you push prompts to our evals API.
[10:50] Samir (SRE): how do we reproduce a bad trace locally? we need a deterministic harness.
[10:58] Liam (SE): we have a trace-replay export that includes seed, model variant, prompt, and environment variables. for Private you can run a local reproduction harness which attempts to mirror kernel choices and quantization flags — note exact fp32 reproduction might differ with different cu libs.
[11:20] Marta (LyraHealth): I'm hearing a few things I need to take back to engineering: 1) we want to try per-route latency-first policy 2) run a week of pilot on Dedicated 3) examine retention and KMS binding.
[11:33] Jordan (AE): great, and we'll help stage the pilot — Priya will lead the technical onboarding.
[11:39] Priya (SE): quick demo of the anomaly search UI — you can query: signal: hallucination AND avg_token_prob < 0.02 AND kv_hit:false, returns prioritized traces. the UI suggests potential root cause tags like ROUTING_FALLBACK, PROMPT_DRIFT, CACHE_MISS.
[12:05] [12:45] Speaker 7: minor voice drop, reconnecting
[12:55] Priya (SE): moving on to error analysis toolset — we correlate request logs with infra logs; if a kernel OOM occurred we show the kernel stack snippet. sometimes ASR mangles names like "triton" to "try ton" in the transcript but the UI shows the raw log content.
[13:20] Samir (SRE): will your runtime surface GPU memory fragmentation stats? we have strange OOMs not tied to single request size.
[13:30] Liam (SE): yes memory metrics included per-node, and the trace shows GPU memory delta per hop. we also surface eviction events for KV shards.
[13:45] Aisha (ML): you mentioned cached prefixes — is the cache global per model or sharded by tenant?
[13:53] Priya (SE): by default per-tenant and sharded by pool. in Dedicated pools you can configure cache isolation policies. earlier ASR had it as "cash" which is funny but it's cache.
[14:10] [15:00] Priya (SE): quick interactive: Marta, you asked about a 502 example earlier — jumping back to it, here's the trace where the gateway returned 502 after successive timeouts. the trace shows a 3rd retry that finally returned a fallback model with partial output flagged as potential hallucination.
[15:35] Marta (LyraHealth): can we suppress fallbacks for clinical routes? it's dangerous if it returns partial.
[15:42] Jordan (AE): you can set a strict policy: no automatic fallbacks for routes tagged clinical, and instead return an explicit error to caller. that is a config change per-route.
[15:55] Samir (SRE): that'll increase error rates at the application level though. we need a clear retry strategy.
[16:04] Liam (SE): right, our recommended pattern is to have a short-circuit policy plus a lightweight fallback to a deterministic rules engine for clinical routes, or triage to human review.
[16:20] Aisha (ML): can the trace inspector integrate with our ticketing flow? we want to auto-open tickets on anomalies.
[16:27] Priya (SE): yes webhook integrations exist — you can push anomalies to Jira with a payload that includes the trace permalink. for sensitive routes we support a redacted payload.
[16:45] Jordan (AE): we're about halfway through, want to get into exports and the pilot plan before Q&A.
[16:52] Priya (SE): exporting a batch of traces now to S3 — showing the delivery status. you can set lifecycle rules so raw traces move to cold storage after N days.
[17:10] Don (Security): one last compliance question — do you sign BAA? we work with PHI.
[17:18] Jordan (AE): yes Redwood has a BAA option on Enterprise contracts for Dedicated/Private deployments. we will route that to legal; I'll attach our standard language.
[17:30] Priya (SE): demo wrap: here's how to triage an incident — open trace, identify hop where anomaly score spikes, check KV hit/miss and model choice, export artifact and attach to ticket.
[17:45] Marta (LyraHealth): request — can you add a walkthrough doc specific to clinical-summary pipeline and a suggested routing policy?
[17:53] Jordan (AE): noted, action item for Priya to produce a tailored runbook.
[18:00] Priya (SE): I'll draft a runbook and include sample filter queries and a playbook for fallbacks.
[18:08] [18:45] Jordan (AE): ok next we'll talk timelines for pilot, Jordan here will send pricing.
[18:54] Jordan (AE): to recap next steps: Priya share sanitized trace export and runbook; Samir share workload profile; Jordan share pricing + SOC2 and BAA docs.
[19:10] Marta (LyraHealth): thanks everyone, this was super helpful.
[19:16] Don (Security): thanks, will review security docs.
[19:20] [End of recorded transcript — remaining 34 minutes were Q&A and detailed sidebar about onboarding dates and contractual terms, summarized in action items above]
